key_insight: A single plasma proteomics test, interpreted with adaptive machine learning, can distinguish malignant from benign adnexal masses without relying on preset biomarker panels.
clinical_relevance: This approach could improve pre-operative triage of ovarian/adnexal masses and reduce unnecessary surgery by adding a blood-based layer to imaging and standard markers.
method: Data-independent-acquisition mass spectrometry measured >1,000 plasma proteins per sample.
ADAPT-MS retrained an ElasticNet model for each sample using the proteins detected.
Performance was tested across discovery, multiple validation cohorts, and an external center.
evidence_signal: In 1,685 total participants across discovery and validation cohorts, the classifier achieved a summary AUC of 0.835, and in matched subsets it improved discrimination when combined with O-RADS to 0.922.
watch_item: This is still a specialized mass-spectrometry workflow that will need independent prospective validation, standardization, and real-world implementation testing before routine use.
paper_title: Differentiating benign from malignant adnexal masses by biomarker-agnostic plasma proteomics using adaptive machine learning
